clue.text: Go steadily or make your Xmas worker walk up and down?

definitions.meaning: to avoid rushing, keeping energy in reserve over a long task

definitions.text: make your Xmas worker walk up and down?
definitions.meaning: read literally: get your own little helper from Santa's workshop to stride to and fro

explanation.surface: A seasonal question: should you take it easy, or have your festive helper pace about?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits as PACE ONE'S ELF: an elf is Santa's Xmas worker, and to pace is to walk up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to work at a sustainable rate rather than burning out early.

clue.text: Give out something you might want to receive this Xmas

definitions.meaning: to hand over formally, as with an award

definitions.text: something you might want to receive this Xmas
definitions.meaning: a gift, as found under the tree

explanation.surface: A seasonal reflection on giving and receiving gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hand over ceremonially; as a noun it is a gift.

clue.text: Xmas food box with bit of tuck that student group wraps

parts.note: a chest is a large box

indicators.note: the student group goes round the letter from tuck, enclosing it

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

indicators.note: only a small piece, the first letter, of the word tuck is used

explanation.surface: A hamper of festive food, with some student society bundling up the snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for snacks and sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasted chestnuts are a traditional seasonal treat, as in the song about an open fire.

clue.text: God is love? That's a racket!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a din is a racket, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A cynic dismisses the slogan 'God is love' as a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a swindle, but here it means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: American's Xmas drink finished up? Turned out Greg tucked into it!

indicators.note: the letters from Greg go inside the reversed word
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: something finished is gone

indicators.note: turned out as in emptied, like pockets: Greg loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the festive drink is all gone, and Greg has been helping himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the synonym in this down clue; 'Turned out' means emptied, like pockets, leaving only Greg's outer letters, which are 'tucked into' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy spiced drink of milk, sugar and beaten eggs, especially popular in the US at the holidays.

clue.text: Nurse with bad acne hospital department initially made better

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of acne are spoilt into a new order
only the opening letter of department is used

explanation.surface: A patient with bad skin is treated by a nurse and a hospital department and improves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges ACNE to ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improved or heightened in quality is said to have been boosted in this way.

clue.text: State of severe cold affected one's ferns, head of zoo held

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the letter from zoo inside them
affected as in disturbed or altered: these letters are rearranged
the first letter of zoo is taken

explanation.surface: A hard frost has damaged someone's garden ferns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges ONE'S FERNS, which is 'held' round the Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the condition of being turned to ice, as in a hard freeze.

clue.text: Flipping costly to lose article like Santa's suit

indicators.note: flipping means the remaining letters are turned round
the article is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: something costly is dear
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that something expensive has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' takes A from DEAR to give DER; 'Flipping' turns that round. 'Flipping' looks like a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is traditionally dressed in a scarlet suit trimmed with white.

clue.text: Queen has browned bread with no topping for Xmas dinner?

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: toast is bread browned under heat

explanation.surface: The monarch eats plain toast without butter or jam at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no topping' looks like butter left off; it removes the first letter from TOAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas dinner is typically a cooked joint of meat or a bird done in the oven.

clue.text: Abandon hope (especially after daughter gets gas)

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for especially behind the D

parts.note: air is a mixture of gases

explanation.surface: A parenthetical warning to give up when one's daughter starts producing wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to lose all hope, the same as giving it up.

clue.text: How Carol says snow settles in Freiburg finally around 6pm?

parts.note: the carol Good King Wenceslas has the snow lying 'deep and crisp and even'

indicators.note: only the last letter of Freiburg is used

explanation.surface: A wintry scene of snow settling in a German city one night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is the Christmas carol Good King Wenceslas.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the day around dusk, from about six o'clock, is this time.

clue.text: After snarfing food endlessly, husband beams and cheers

indicators.note: snarfing means gobbling up, so the other letters take in what is left of food

parts.note: rays are beams of light

indicators.note: food loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A husband wolfs down his food, beaming and cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves OO from FOOD, which H and RAYS take in.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of joy or approval, plural, are expressions of celebration like cheers.

clue.text: Worries escalate after turkey's served for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first letters, taken from the four following words

explanation.surface: Anxieties rise once the Christmas turkey has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' suggests a first course but takes initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble or nag at someone, as in 'what's bugging you?', is this verb's idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Bloomer associated with Xmas in Thailand misbehaving with opiates

indicators.note: misbehaving signals that the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A tale of drug-taking and misbehaviour in Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges IN, T and OPIATES. 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This red-leaved Mexican plant is a seasonal decoration sold everywhere in December.

clue.text: Having saved one grand, relished travelling for Xmas jaunt?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the I and G inside them
travelling signals that the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is short for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone put by a thousand and enjoyed a festive trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges RELISHED to SLEHRIDE, and 'Having saved' puts IG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip on a horse-drawn snow sledge is the classic winter outing of Christmas songs.

clue.text: In this way son left Boxing Day party at the end? On the contrary!

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, as in putting things in a box
this reverses the enclosure as read, so the day and party letters go round S and L instead

parts.note: Thu is the abbreviation for Thursday

indicators.note: only the final letter of party is used

explanation.surface: A son leaves the Boxing Day party late, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: As read, S and L would be 'Boxing' THU and Y; 'On the contrary' flips that, so THU...Y goes round SL. Boxing Day is the British holiday on 26 December.
explanation.definitionFit: A rather affected adverb meaning thus or so.

clue.text: Hot duke chasing soldiers? Always a few on the pull at Xmas!

definitions.text: a few on the pull at Xmas!

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the next pieces come after the soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
hot as in fashionable, in
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A randy aristocrat chases soldiers, and a few people are always out looking for a date at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the pull' is British slang for seeking a sexual partner; here it means hauling the sleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's sleigh is pulled by a team of these antlered animals.

clue.text: They make shots bigger in flipping Tyneside (and beers with drop of rye in there!)

indicators.note: flipping turns the two letters round

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

indicators.note: the letter from rye goes inside the beers

parts.note: lagers are beers

indicators.note: a drop, the first letter, of rye

explanation.surface: A drinking scene on Tyneside with beers and a shot of rye whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses NE to EN. 'shots' suggests drinks; it means photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkroom devices that project a negative to produce bigger photographic prints.

clue.text: Xmas illumination not well-ventilated? A knight should open that window

indicators.note: the A and N go into the opening of what remains
not means the synonym for well-ventilated is left out

parts.note: fairy lights are strings of small bulbs on the tree
an airy room is well-ventilated
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A stuffy room with festive lights, and a knight told to open the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AIRY from FAIRY LIGHT to leave FLIGHT, which 'A knight' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: A small window above a door, often semicircular with radiating bars like a fan.

clue.text: Around four, cook large feast for Christmas Day?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters plus L go round the numeral
to cook the books is to falsify them, so the letters of feast are rearranged

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone plans to cook a big festive feast at about four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like a literal kitchen instruction but rearranges feast into FESTA; L follows, and the whole goes 'Around' the Roman four.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of celebration or holiday; Christmas is one such example.

clue.text: Sheepish complaint climbing hill and also peak of fells

indicators.note: in a down clue the peak is the top, first letter of fells
in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
too means also

explanation.surface: A sheep's ailment on a hill walk through the fells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses TORTOO to OOTROT. 'Sheepish' suggests embarrassment; it means of sheep. Fells are hills of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacterial infection of the hooves in sheep, making them lame.

clue.text: No substance in pious charity songs like Millennium Prayer?

indicators.note: the inside of pious is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A cynic sneers at hollow charity singles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Prayer was Cliff Richard's 1999 Christmas number one, the Lord's Prayer sung to Auld Lang Syne.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred songs or hymns, as in the Biblical book; the Lord's Prayer set to music is akin.

clue.text: Bit of rust in jet on small wind generators this time of year?

definitions.text: wind generators this time of year?

indicators.note: the letter from rust is placed inside the synonym for jet

parts.note: a spout is a jet of liquid

indicators.note: only a small piece, the first letter, of rust

explanation.surface: Some rust on a jet sitting on small wind turbines in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts S below. 'wind generators' suggests turbines; Brussels sprouts famously cause flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels sprouts, the Christmas vegetable, are notorious for producing wind.

clue.text: Victor half-heartedly bears temperature in the cold season

indicators.note: bears as in carries, so the shortened word holds T
the heart of the synonym is a doubled letter, and half of it is dropped

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A lacklustre champion copes with the temperature as the cold sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' turns WINNER into WINER, which 'bears' T.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest of the four seasons, between autumn and spring.

clue.text: After losing head, Catholic MP drunkenly wins hearts of viewers

indicators.note: wins means gains, taking the H inside
drunkenly signals the letters reel into a new order
Catholic is used once its first letter has gone

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A beheaded Catholic MP, drunk, wins over viewers' hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' rearranges ATHOLIC and MP to OPTHALMIC, which 'wins' H. 'viewers' means eyes, not TV audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the eyes, the organs we see with.

clue.text: Xmas decoration completely lacking in width

indicators.note: lacking means the W is taken away

parts.note: wholly means completely

explanation.surface: A festive decoration with no breadth at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Its prickly leaves and red berries are a traditional seasonal decoration.

clue.text: Three Republicans put on first side of Baby, It's Cold Outside!

indicators.note: the first side of a word is its opening edge, so only the initial letter of Baby is taken

parts.note: R is short for Republican, so three of them give three Rs

explanation.surface: Three Republicans put on side one of the record Baby, It's Cold Outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' in an across clue places RRR after B. Baby, It's Cold Outside is a festive duet.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation mimics shivering, as one says on stepping into freezing air.

clue.text: Transportation company over in Germany

definitions.meaning: the German word meaning over or above

explanation.surface: A taxi firm operating across Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The ride-hailing firm took its name from the German preposition meaning above or beyond.

clue.text: Heaving pub expends its last gallon after large Latin men returned

indicators.note: after places the shortened pub and G behind the reversed letters
returned means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the pub word loses its final letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A packed pub runs out of its last gallon of beer after large Latin men come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LLOR into ROLL; 'expends its last' trims INN to IN. 'Heaving' looks like crowded; it means swaying.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is pitching and swaying in a swell is said to be heaving.

clue.text: Scene in story about Balthazar originally taking gold

indicators.note: the story goes around the letter from Balthazar

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: the first letter of Balthazar

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: The Nativity story of Balthazar, one of the Magi, bringing gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Balthazar is traditionally one of the three wise men, though the gift of gold is usually Melchior's.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking, picture-like arrangement of people, as in a nativity tableau.

clue.text: Lad loses head after the opening of this!

definitions.text: Lad loses head after the opening of this!

indicators.note: after places the trimmed lad behind that opening letter
the opening, first letter, of the word this
the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy goes wild with excitement after unwrapping his Christmas gift.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue pictures a child losing his head on opening a plaything; 'opening' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaything is exactly what would send a youngster wild on Christmas morning.

clue.text: Endeavours to go in for things one might win on radio

parts.note: to enter is to go in

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so the word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: prizes are what one wins

explanation.surface: Advice to try your luck in radio competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: PRISES (levers open) is spelt by ear from 'prizes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold projects or undertakings, a synonym of ventures.
